source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, about 2.2 percent of Virginia's 1,639.4 MW of disclosed data center capacity.

The facility is one of only 26 Virginia sites that publish a megawatt figure, out of 332 mapped. That gap is the real finding. Published capacity in Virginia is a small, self-selected sample, so any state total built from it undercounts the actual load. Ashburn VA7 ranks 14th of those 26, which places it in the middle of the disclosed field rather than at its top.

The 36 MW converts to roughly 900 racks at 40 kW per rack, and roughly 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators depending on configuration. Those figures come from assumptions about rack density and training power ratios, not from the operator. The 125,000 square feet of technical space is the only physical measure published here, and it says nothing about how much power the building can actually draw.

What the data does not cover is decisive. There is no grid connection, no interconnection capacity, no power purchase agreement, and no statement of whether the space is reserved for AI workloads. A facility's IT capacity is a ceiling set by its own equipment, not by what the utility will deliver. Without the interconnection figure, 36 MW describes the building, not the constraint.
